recipes.name: Roasted Carrot Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds carrots, peeled and thinly sliced on the diagonal
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (4 ounce) package crumbled Danish blue cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Combine carrots, almonds, and garlic in a mixing bowl. Drizzle with olive oil, then season to taste with salt and pepper. Spread on an ungreased baking sheet.
Bake carrots in the preheated oven until soft and the edges turn brown, about 30 minutes. Remove and allow to cool to room temperature.

Once cool, return carrots to the mixing bowl, and drizzle with honey and vinegar; toss until coated. Add cranberries and blue cheese; toss again until evenly mixed. Combine with the arugula and serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Carrot Salad
raw_recipe.description: This amazing carrot salad made with thinly sliced roasted carrots, honey, almonds, cranberries, and blue cheese is perfect for parties and potlucks.

review.reviewBody: One of the best recipes I have ever made from this site! This was a huge success at our dinner party last night. I used Gorgonzola (husband doesn't like blue cheese). Doubled the garlic because we are big fans and used spring mix for Arugula because the market was out of just Arugula. Thanks Morgan for sharing my favorite new recipe!

I love this! This is just enough “elevated” for great hosting presentation, yet familiar enough to be friendly for most guests. I used Tri colored carrots and liked that added pop of color. The garlic does get a bit charred and bitter, so I may toast the almonds and garlic separately in a pan next time (yes, there will be a next time for sure)! I realized I didn’t actually have any honey, so I subbed (real) maple syrup instead. My grocery store was out of arugula (why did I shop on a Sunday afternoon?!) so I used baby spinach. I don’t care for/have a use for dried cranberries on their own, but do love a salad toppings mix with them a toasted almonds, so I used that. Next time, I will also roast some beets with the carrots. This is delightful; thanks for the recipe!

I loved this recipe, but then any roasted veggie is a BIG yummy for me. As is, the recipe is more of a side veggie dish with the arugala acting much like a parsley addition...and great. As a Salad, I found it needed more Arugala. Even with adding more Arugala, the suggested dressing amount was sufficient to dress the added greens. I toasted my almonds separately and added at the end/serving, as I wanted to retain their crunch texture. Not only is this Super tasty, it HAS to be a really healthful recipe... just do not tell anyone, how healthy and EZ!

I was surprised at the mix of flavors but they absolutely worked! I deviated away from the recipe but kept the integrity (i.e., used full-size carrots, used cane syrup rather than honey, power greens rather than arugula). My husband ate two huge servings, so this recipe will really serve about two persons. My husband used a mandolin to slice the carrots, and they were gorgeous. Thanks so much for submitting this recipe!

This was a great salad! I cheated and used precut carrots to save time, and I'm not sure I would do that next time. It took my carrots 45 minutes to get soft and browned and therefore, got a bit dry. Next time I think I may try doubling the honey and vinegar, as my salad was a bit dry, overall. The flavor, though, was unique and delicious and my husband and I thoroughly enjoyed it! Thanks for sharing your recipe!

I LOVE this recipe!!! 5 star with no adjustments, but I have made it several times now and have learned a few useful tips- 1) always make 2-4x the dressing suggested. Tossing a little w the carrots after they've cooled and then the greens separately before plating helps you use less, otherwise it falls to the bottom and you need to add more. (I should note that I always use a platter rather than a bowl so the carrots are the star in the middle and don't mix everything together) 2) I also add extra blue cheese- I've only ever used Humbolt Fog because I love it and feel it's a great blue cheese for even the pickiest eaters. 3) Be careful with the garlic. The second time I made this salad I added too much and it ruined the flavor profile. 4) I love arugula, but the salad can be boosted with a little chopped romain mixed in as well. It adds extra crunch and helps to catch the dressing. This salad was a huge hit every time I made it and I will continue to use this recipe several times a year.

OMG. And I do not say that often in my reviews. I should have done 10# of roasted carrots. I roasted the carrots in my new tabletop convection oven in 2 layers until they started browning. The flavors were all so amazing together. I have to make another batch now and leave in the frig for salads. I served it with smoked brisket but I could just eat the salad for a whole meal for a week. Thanks so much for this recipe!

A W E S O M E
Went looking for a carrot recipe since I had a large bag of carrots and knew they weren't going to get used up before vacay. 
Found this and saw it had some ingredients I just love like cheese and arugula. (I'm not a huge fan of cooked carrots.)
This was great and I did take others' advice on decreasing and/or increasing some of the ingredients and roasting the almonds separately. I also went w gorgonzola. 
I prepped the carrots first drizzling w oil and adding salt and pepper. Threw it in the oven while I minced the garlic. Threw the carrots back in the bowl and mixed in the garlic and back in the oven. Carrots cooked great at 30 minutes. 
Easy to make. Def roast almonds separately so they are perfectly roasted because you'll pick up the nutty flavor in the salad.

This was delicious. I didn't have blue cheese, so I used feta instead. I scaled this down to a quarter, and used 1.5 cups of salad greens just on my plate. The full recipe calls for only two cups, so if you split that 6 ways, you'll only have 1/3 cup of greens. I felt like it needed much more for the base which is why I used so much. The only arugula I could find was in a mix of baby spinach and arugula and I wasn't about to pick them out. Watch that oven though as it only took 20 minutes in my oven and some of the carrots and almonds on the perimeter of the sheet tray were starting to burn. I'm glad I smelled them and decided to check on them just because, or they would have been unsalvageable had they roasted another 10 minutes. That is a matter of knowing your equipment, and I know my oven tends to cook hotter and usually things take a few minutes less than indicated. I'm not going to fault the recipe as the submitter's oven may take the full 30 minutes. Regardless, this was fantastic. The sweet carrots, the toasted almonds, the chewy cranberries, the savory garlic and touch of tart and tangy vinegar and honey, all the flavors and textures had a party for my tastebuds. I've never eaten cold cooked carrots before, but this worked well. The salad part was dry though and really needed some dressing. It only called for the honey/vinegar to be tossed with the carrots and the salad could benefit from some too. I liked the sharp peppery bite from the arugula, but I am also glad it was mixed with spinach as all arugula might have been too much for me, and I know all spinach is too much for me. I cleaned my plate and I will definitely make this again. Thanks for sharing this.

Yes, this is a great recipe! I was excited to hear that it is inspired by that carrot salad at the wonderful Farmer's Market in Woodstock, VT--we frequented it often when visiting family there in Woodstock. I have made this several times in the last month! The last time I made it I roasted asparagus with the carrots and added a just a smidgeon of roasted sesame oil just before serving.

Excellent dish -made it twice, and was a huge hit both times. Very easy to improvise with the recipe - Replaced the cranberries with pomegranate seeds and cheese with Parmesan once, second time used a mild roquefort and mixed baby leaves instead of arugula.
This will definitely go in our summer salad rotation!! It is DELICIOUS! I did double the dressing though.

Delicious! Made this as described except roasted the carrots alone for 20 minutes, then added the almonds and garlic for the last 10 minutes (to keep them from getting too brown). Outcome was excellent. Received rave reviews at the potluck. A keeper!
I didn't like the arugula very much so I didn't add much. The rest all went well together.

Loved it! This recipe looked interesting and worth a try and I'm so glad I tried it. Will be making this again and again! The dressing wasn't enough to coat everything, so I added more olive oil, honey, and cider vinegar. I also used simmered cranberries instead of dried because that was what I had on hand. Will use them again as they added more to the dressing and made it a nice color!

This salad recipe is delicious! I absolutely love the roasted carrots on top of the salad. We used a mixture of spinach and lettuce instead of arugula. I also substituted feta for the blue cheese. This was easy to make and you could definitely make tweaks to your preference. The only thing that I will do differently next time is to double the honey/vinegar mixture. We'll be adding it to our salad rotation.

Crunchy, Chewy and Jam Packed with Your Favorite Flavors! Made this today and took it to the season's first pool party. It was a splashing success!! If you love the robustness of garlic, blue cheese, honey and arugula and the freshness of carrots, cranberries, and the crunch of almonds this salad is for you!! Amazingly, I did change a thing about this recipe. I will say that my new oven is running hot so the almonds got a little toastier than I would have liked. Watch the temp and perhaps reduce to 375 for 25 minutes if you run hot like me.
This was simple to make. Hubs and I both liked it. I served it alongside salmon and used mixed greens instead of the arugula. Will definitely keep this recipe in the rotation.

So good that I had to make two nights in a row! I did take a suggestion from the reviews and used hot honey and balsamic to dress the salad, delicious! I also swapped in feta for the blue cheese (personal preference). Served with grilled steak. Definitely going into my regular rotation!
Delicious!
